newsitem.title: KUWAIT: British minister in Kuwait for talks on ties, arms.
newsitem.headline: British minister in Kuwait for talks on ties, arms.

text.p: British Foreign Office Minister Derek Fatchett arrived in Kuwait on Monday to discuss the future of ties between the oil-rich Gulf Arab state and Britain's first Labour government in 18 years.

Diplomatic sources said Fatchett was expected to discuss obstacles facing an order for British Aerospace Plc Sea Skua missiles and express unease at reports that a Kuwaiti military committee had recommended a Chinese artillery gun over offers by South Africa, the United States and Britain.

He is also expected to stress that Labour, which came to power in May, is also firmly committed to the security of Kuwait like the previous conservative government which played a central role in forming the multinational military coalition which forced Iraq out of Kuwait in the 1991 Gulf War.

Fatchett, the first minister in the new government to visit Kuwait, has already held talks in Britain with Kuwait's Crown Prince and Prime Minister Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al-Sabah and Defence Minister Sheikh Salem Sabah al-Salem al-Sabah.
